notes.meaning: David calls God's people to notice how wonderful and delightful it is when they live together in peace. The word brothers includes family members, fellow believers, and all who share the same faith and worship. Many things in life are good without being pleasant, or pleasant without being good, but true unity brings both. When God's people live in harmony, it brings genuine joy to everyday life.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars think the Hebrew wording points to a time after the exile in Babylon, so the psalm may be later than David. They read it as a song about God's people gathering from all over the land for worship at the great feasts.

notes.meaning: Unity is compared to the fragrant, holy oil poured out when Aaron was set apart as the high priest. This rich olive oil, mixed with sweet spices, was poured so generously that it ran down his beard and onto the collar of his sacred robe. Just as that oil covered Aaron completely with fragrance, brotherly love spreads God's sweet and refreshing blessing over the whole community.

Unity is also compared to the heavy dew that gathers on snowy Mount Hermon and refreshes the dry hills around Jerusalem. In a hot and thirsty land, cool dew quietly gives life to the grass and crops every morning. Where God's people live in concord, the Lord commands His richest blessing, granting them life with Him that lasts forever.
